sentences.text: The holotype specimen — the specific fossil the species is based on — contains bones from the arm, leg, pelvic girdle, thorax, and neck.
This adult animal is estimated to have measured between 2.5 and 2.8 meters in size.
When described in 2021, Plesiopharos was the most complete and oldest known plesiosaur from the Iberian Peninsula.
The genus name means "close lighthouse" because the holotype was discovered near a lighthouse in São Pedro de Moel.
Fossils were found by collectors António Silva and Vítor Teixeira and donated to the Lourinhã Museum in 2017.
Plesiopharos moelensis is classified as a basal member of the superfamily Plesiosauroidea.
Plesiopharos lived during the Sinemurian age in layers of the Coimbra Formation found in Portugal.
The animal lived between 199.5 and 192.9 million years ago.
